Which accounts in a row's log are the channel

log_channel_accounts.Rd

The account that holds the round's token, as the machine that runs the round configures it (more than one while the token changes hands), and nobody else; or, where it is not configured, every account that wrote a field only the channel is meant to write, register_channel_fields(), in the row's current life. Callers drop the channel's events by account, and read the answer one more way through log_channel_unknown(): without the configuration, two accounts writing those fields leave the log unable to say which writes are the round's.

Usage

log_channel_accounts(events, record, channel_account = NULL)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured.

Value

A character vector of usernames. With channel_account, every spelling of those accounts the row's log carries, and each configured name the log does not carry; nobody else. Without, the authors of the channel fields, empty when no event wrote one of them.

Details

It has to be recognized by the account and not by the event. REDCap logs only the fields an import changed, so when the round writes back a username it resolved and the verdict has not moved, the event carries username alone – an intent field, written by the channel, with nothing in the event itself to say so.

The account is configured, decided on 2026-10-17. Recognized by what it writes alone, the channel is whoever wrote a channel field, and the import right is open to the referents: one who imports owned_by on a colleague's new row, before the round has written on it, would be the only "channel" of that row. Named by the configuration, the channel is the round's account even on a row where it has not written yet, and a write of a channel field by any other account is ignored (decided on 2026-10-17, replacing the ambiguity this function used to answer). Such a write no longer makes the row ambiguous: the log never forgets it, so an ambiguous row was held for ever, even one whose referent imported by mistake a CSV carrying the channel's columns; and with the account named there is nothing to guess, since the owner comes only from that account's writes of owned_by, log_owner(). A write of an intent field by another account stays a change of its author, log_change_authors(), the channel's columns beside it or not.

More than one account can be configured, for the day the account that holds the token changes (decided on 2026-10-17): every one of them is the channel, so the old account's writes, its passages of owned_by among them, stay believed while it is listed.

The configured names are typed by hand on the machine, so they are compared without regard to case, and answered with the spelling the log carries when the log carries it. Without them, NULL, the answer is the authors of the channel fields, as before the account was configured: what the round judges does not change for a caller that does not pass it, and log_owner() believes no write of owned_by.
